title: The Horse and His Rider
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Young Man, who fancied himself something of a horseman, mounted a Horse which had not been properly broken in, and was exceedingly difficult to control. No sooner did the Horse feel his weight in the saddle than he bolted, and nothing would stop him. A friend of the Rider's met him in the road in his headlong career, and called out, "Where are you off to in such a hurry?" To which he, pointing to the Horse, replied, "I've no idea: ask him."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Young Man see himself?
options: As something of a horseman
As a skilled blacksmith
As a cautious traveller
As a poor rider who needed practice

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was true of the Horse the Young Man mounted?
options: It was old and slow
It had not been properly broken in and was hard to control
It belonged to his friend
It had thrown other riders many times before

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Horse do as soon as it felt the Young Man's weight?
options: It reared up and threw him off
It bolted and nothing would stop him
It refused to move at all
It walked calmly down the road

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who met the Rider in the road during his headlong ride?
options: A stranger on foot
A friend of the Rider's
A rival horseman
The Horse's original owner

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the friend call out to the Rider?
options: "Stop that horse before it hurts someone!"
"Where are you off to in such a hurry?"
"You should never have mounted that horse!"
"Do you need help getting down?"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Rider reply when asked where he was going?
options: "To the market, as always"
"Nowhere in particular"
"I've no idea: ask him"
"I am trying to reach the stable"

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "bolted" mean in "he bolted, and nothing would stop him"?
options: Fastened himself in place
Ate very quickly
Ran off suddenly and uncontrollably
Fell asleep instantly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Rider's answer, "ask him," reveal about who is really in control?
options: The Rider is joking and is actually fully in control
The Horse, not the Rider, is now deciding where they go
The friend is expected to stop the Horse himself
The Rider has decided to turn back home

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what problem did the Horse have before the Young Man mounted it?
options: It had not been properly broken in
It had gone lame in one leg
It had never been ridden before at all
It was too old to be ridden safely

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the friend meet the Rider?
options: In the road
At the stable
In a nearby field
At the Rider's house

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "headlong career" mean in "met him in the road in his headlong career"?
options: A slow, cautious walk
A reckless, uncontrolled dash
A planned route home
A brief pause to rest

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "fancied" mean in "who fancied himself something of a horseman"?
options: Decorated elaborately
Genuinely doubted
Considered or imagined himself to be
Was told by others that he was

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is it ironic that the Young Man thought himself a skilled horseman?
options: He chose a horse that turned out to be completely beyond his control
He had never actually ridden a horse before this
He was actually a very experienced rider who got unlucky
He was riding on a dare from his friend

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A self-assured rider mounts an unbroken horse that bolts, leaving him with no control over where he is going
A skilled horseman calmly rides through town greeting friends
A rider trains a wild horse until it becomes obedient
A friend warns a rider not to mount a horse, and he listens
